title: FinVeriQA: Financial Research Agents for Question Answering: Routing, Retrieval, MCP Tool Use, and Provenance-Aware Evidence Verification
abstract: arXiv:2611.25071v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) write fluent financial analyses but miscompute ratios, recall stale prices, and route questions to the wrong tool with high confidence. We ask which component should do each job in a financial question-answering assistant, and study it with FinVeriQA, an open-source multi-agent research prototype over SEC filings and live market data: a compact typed-decision model (Laya) routes each question and screens out advice requests, Python computes every number, retrieval and tools fetch evidence, Mistral-7B writes a cited answer, a code validator checks that cited IDs exist and that numbers match computed notes, and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server exposes the pipeline. In live experiments, Laya routed better than Mistral-7B (0.85 vs. 0.52; overall 0.86 vs. 0.68, McNemar p = 0.0003); a 12B Mistral decided no better, and DeepSeek-R1-8B decided better (0.79 vs. 0.68, p = 0.0192) but about 9.9 times more slowly.

translated_title: FinVeriQA：面向问答的金融研究智能体：路由、检索、MCP工具使用与溯源感知的证据验证
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）能够写出流畅的金融分析，但会算错比率、引用过时的价格数据，并且高置信度地将问题路由到错误的工具。我们探讨在金融问答助手系统中，哪个组件应该承担哪项任务，并通过FinVeriQA——一个基于SEC文件与实时市场数据的开源多智能体研究原型——来研究这一问题：一个紧凑的类型化决策模型（Laya）负责路由每个问题并筛选出投资建议类请求，Python负责计算每一个数字，检索与工具负责获取证据，Mistral-7B撰写带引用的回答，一个代码验证器检查引用的ID是否存在以及数字是否与计算出的笔记相匹配，并通过模型上下文协议（MCP）服务器将整条流水线对外暴露。在实时实验中，Laya的路由表现优于Mistral-7B（0.85 vs. 0.52；总体0.86 vs. 0.68，McNemar检验 p = 0.0003）；一个12B参数的Mistral决策能力并未更优，而DeepSeek-R1-8B决策表现更好（0.79 vs. 0.68，p = 0.0192），但速度慢约9.9倍。
tldr: 该论文提出FinVeriQA——一个基于SEC文件与实时市场数据的开源多智能体金融问答系统，其核心创新在于用紧凑的专用决策模型Laya进行问题路由与建议过滤，配合Python精确计算、MCP工具检索与溯源感知的证据验证，实验证明小型决策模型的路由性能可显著超越大型语言模型，并在决策准确性与推理速度之间取得最佳权衡。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces FinVeriQA, an open-source multi-agent financial QA system over SEC filings and live market data, whose key contribution is showing that a compact typed-decision model (Laya) substantially outperforms larger LLMs at question routing and advice filtering, while Python-based computation, MCP tool retrieval, and provenance-aware evidence verification ensure accurate, cited answers.
